saints.name: Saint Nino, Equal-to-Apostles
saints.title: Saint Nino, Equal-to-the-Apostles and Enlightener of Georgia
saints.notes: Saint Nino brought Christianity to Georgia (Iberia) around 327 AD. Born in Cappadocia, she carried a cross of vine branches bound with her own hair. She healed Queen Nana and converted King Mirian III, making Georgia one of the first Christian kingdoms. She is depicted with a distinctive vine-wood cross with drooping arms, still the symbol of the Georgian Church.

notes: Julian January 14 corresponds to Gregorian January 27.

saints.name: Saint Shio Mgvime
saints.title: Saint Shio of Mgvime, One of the Thirteen Syrian Fathers
saints.notes: One of the Thirteen Syrian Fathers who came to Georgia from Antioch in the 6th century. Shio founded the Shio-Mgvime cave monastery near Mtskheta, which became a major center of Georgian monasticism. His asceticism was so severe he lived as a hermit in a cave, sustained by miraculous provision. One of the most revered founders of the Georgian Church.

notes: Julian May 9 corresponds to Gregorian May 22.

saints.name: Blessed Queen Tamara
saints.title: Blessed Queen Tamara of Georgia, The Great
saints.notes: Queen Tamara (1160–1213) led Georgia to its Golden Age as the dominant power in the Caucasus. A pious ruler, she commissioned churches, supported monasteries on Athos, and her court fostered the golden age of Georgian literature, including Shota Rustaveli's The Knight in the Panther's Skin. Venerated as a saint by the Georgian Orthodox Church.

notes: Julian May 1 corresponds to Gregorian May 14.
